cars.variant: Black Bess, Labourdette two-seater — 1913 delivery and museum reference
cars.specification_market: Original Type 18 production-road sporting family, selected Black Bess Labourdette two-seater at Louwman Museum, 1913 delivery reference. Ten attributes use the historical Type 18 paragraphs in the English 10 April 2014 manufacturer release; three use the museum description of the same car. Keep the manufacturer 5-litre displacement rounded and museum output quoted as 100 hp with no inferred test standard or rpm. No exact displacement conversion or equation between museum hp, English PS and French CV is asserted. English wheelbase 2.45 m conflicts with French 2.54 m, so wheelbase is omitted. Manufacturer 160-km/h and museum 150-km/h claims are not measured performance and are omitted. Chain-drive wording differs in specificity between languages; no assumed camshaft or final-drive function is added. Group Type 18 years, coachwork, chassis and racing appearances once. The 2014 Veyron Black Bess cosmetic tribute, dedicated racing machines, replicas and additional individual Type 18 survivors are not admitted.
cars.summary: The original Bugatti Type 18 represents the early high-performance road car through its large four-cylinder engine, overhead camshaft, three-valve cylinders and sporting engineering. The documented Black Bess road example, delivered to aviation pioneer Roland Garros, links that engineering to an enduring part of Bugatti history. Count the Type 18 road family once; limited production and celebrity ownership alone are not admission reasons, and the later Veyron tribute creates no extra historical car.

sources.title: Les Legendes de Bugatti: Black Bess premiere, 10 April 2014 — historical Type 18 and technical-description sections
sources.source_type: Original manufacturer historical account and explicit technical description
sources.notes: Historical Type 18 context, customer-road identity, 1913 two-seater delivery and complete historical technical-description sections read. Ten attributes map here: four in-line cylinders, 5 litres, 100-mm bore, 160-mm stroke, three crank bearings, overhead camshaft, three valves per cylinder, four forward gears/reverse, 1.25-m track and two seats. English and French versions compared: wheelbase 2.45 versus 2.54 m is omitted. English 100/over-100 PS and French over-100 CV do not become a converted museum hp figure. No output rpm, top speed, exclusive fastest-road-car claim, totals, aviation flight-year assertion, chain-drive function or naming etymology imported. Modern W16 Veyron engine, carbon body, gold trim, leather, price and performance data are not Type 18 specifications.

facts.title: A distinctive two-seat layout
facts.explanation: Louwman Museum identifies the coachwork as Henri Labourdette and describes the bucket seats as angled and staggered so driver and passenger do not obstruct each other. This describes the selected Black Bess collection reference rather than universal coachwork on every Type 18.
